note: OTHMODE Skill / MCP trust policy (SKILL-TRUST-0). Turns scanner results — NVIDIA SkillSpector, Gitleaks, NVIDIA SkillEvaluator Tier 1, and the gateway's mcp-registry-check snapshot — into exactly one OTHMODE decision: ACCEPT, REVIEW or BLOCK. The most restrictive applicable rule wins. Evaluated by projects/command-center/reference/othmode/trust/policy.js; deterministic, offline, and unit-tested. Invariants no configuration can relax: a missing or failed REQUIRED scanner is never ACCEPT (scanner_failure only chooses between BLOCK and REVIEW); an unparseable or unrecognised result is never ACCEPT; SkillSpector DO_NOT_INSTALL is always BLOCK.

skillspector.note: SkillSpector reports CAUTION for a zero-score, issue-free skill whenever its analysis is 'partial'. With clean_caution_is_accept the policy accepts such a skill ONLY when every partial reason is listed in benign_partial_reasons (an unresolved local path mention in the prose) and no file was left uninspected; any other partial reason — malformed manifest, uninspected files, size ceilings — stays REVIEW.

gitleaks.note: A detected credential pattern blocks. The ledger records rule id, file, line and fingerprint only — never the matched value.

skillevaluator.note: The security check is deliberately NOT in `checks`: it would run SkillSpector a second time. code-integrity is not in `checks` on this host because Semgrep is not installed there and SkillEvaluator marks the whole check INCOMPLETE without it; add it (and Semgrep) when the host has the memory headroom. SCHEMA/LICENSE/QUALITY/SCRIPT_LINT findings are recorded as advisory: this repository's MYTHOS ORIGINAL skills carry no metadata.author, which the default external profile rates HIGH, and that is a publication convention, not a security signal.

mcp.note: MCP trust is a separate layer over the gateway registry check (registration is a claim; the snapshot is the measurement). An extra tool the registry never declared is the tool-poisoning shape this layer can see today; description-level prompt injection needs a scanner that reads tool descriptions and is recorded as the next phase.

scan.baseline_note: The only REVIEW → ACCEPT path for a triaged SkillSpector finding: record it, with a reason, in this Git-reviewed baseline (skillspector baseline <skill> --no-llm -o <file> --reason ...; see upstream docs/SUPPRESSION.md), then rescan. Suppressed findings stay listed in the scan report and in the ledger summary (suppressed count). Absent file = no suppression.
scan.note: Binaries resolve on PATH (uv tool installs to ~/.local/bin) or via SKILL_TRUST_<SCANNER>_BIN. Scanners run with a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, LANG, TMPDIR) — never the caller's credentials — and SkillSpector always with --no-llm: no network, no provider key.
